The [[NBA Finals]] is the annual championship series for the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) held at the conclusion of [[NBA playoffs|its postseason]]. All NBA Finals have been played in a [[Playoff format#Best-of-seven playoff|best-of-seven format]], and are contested between the winners of the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] and the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] (prior to 1971 it was played between division playoff winners), except in {{nbafy|1950}} when the [[Eastern Division (NBA)|Eastern Division]] champion faced the winner between the [[Western Division (NBA)|Western]] and [[Central Division (NBA)|Central Division]] champions. From 1946 through 1949, when the league was known as the [[Basketball Association of America]] (BAA), the playoffs were a three-stage tournament where the two semifinal winners played each other in the finals.<ref>{{cite book |last=Rosen |first=Charley |year=2008 |title=The First Tip-Off: The Incredible Story of the Birth of the NBA |url=https://archive.org/details/firsttipoffincre00rose|url-access=limited |publisher=Mc-Graw Hill |pages=[https://archive.org/details/firsttipoffincre00rose/page/n223 211]–212 |isbn=978-0-07-148785-6}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Anderson |first1=Corrie |first2=Rob |last2=Reheuser |year=2006 |title=Sporting News Official 2006–2007 NBA Guide |publisher=Sporting News Books |isbn=978-0-89204-854-0|display-authors=etal}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Brown |first=Donald H. |year=2007 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BoSQqvcuTXEC |title=A Best of Basketball Story |publisher=AuthorHouse |pages=4–5 |isbn=978-1-4343-4193-8}}</ref> The winning team of the series receives the [[Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy]], which has been awarded since [[1977 NBA Finals|1977]] (between [[1947 BAA Finals|1947]] and [[1976 NBA Finals|1976]] the winning team received the [[Walter A. Brown Trophy]]).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://people.com/sports/larry-obrien-championship-trophy-what-to-know-about-iconic-award/|title=What to Know About the NBA's Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy, Created by Tiffany & Co.|first1=Nicholas|last1=Rice|magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]]|publisher=[[Dotdash Meredith]]|location=[[New York City|New York]]|date=July 8, 2021|access-date=December 20, 2021|archive-date=December 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220144025/https://people.com/sports/larry-obrien-championship-trophy-what-to-know-about-iconic-award/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Champions==
[[File:BostonCelticsChampionshipBanners.jpg|thumb|upright=1.25|The [[Boston Celtics]] have won the most championships of any NBA team. Shown are the championship banners hanging in their home arena, [[TD Garden]].]]
The most recent champions are the [[New York Knicks]], who won their first championship since [[1973 NBA Finals|1973]]. The [[Boston Celtics]] have won the most championships of any team in the league at 18.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Higgins |first=Jack |date=October 18, 2024 |title='Raising 18': All 18 Celtics championship teams |url=https://www.nba.com/news/raising-18-all-18-celtics-championship-teams |access-date=January 22, 2025 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> {{As of|2026}}, the Eastern champions have a 42–38 advantage in NBA titles over the Western champions. The [[1949–50 Minneapolis Lakers season|1949–50 Minneapolis Lakers]], who won the [[1950 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], are counted in the Eastern versus Western champions record as they played that sole season in the Central Division before returning to the Western Division.

* The first parentheses in the ''Western champions'' and ''Eastern champions'' columns indicate the teams' playoff seed. The second parentheses indicate the number of times that teams have appeared in an NBA Finals as well as each respective team's NBA Finals record to date.
